webhooks.name: ClusterQueueWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Defaults and validates ClusterQueue resources. The mutating webhook adds a ResourceInUse finalizer on creation, while the validating webhook enforces correctness of resource groups (no duplicate resources or flavors, non-negative quantities), borrowing/lending limits (must be nil when no cohort, lending must not exceed nominal quota), namespace selector labels, admission check configuration (disallows setting both AdmissionChecks and AdmissionChecksStrategy), preemption policy consistency, and fair sharing settings.

webhooks.name: ClusterQueueWebhook-webhook

webhooks.name: JobSetWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating webhook for JobSet resources that defaults suspension state (suspending jobs managed by Kueue), assigns a default local queue label, defaults the managedBy field for MultiKueue, and validates queue-name immutability, topology requests on replicated jobs, and standard Kueue job constraints on create and update.

webhooks.name: JobSetWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating webhook for JobSet resources that defaults suspension state (suspending jobs managed by Kueue), assigns a default local queue label, defaults the managedBy field for MultiKueue, and validates queue-name immutability, topology requests on replicated jobs, and standard Kueue job constraints on create and update.

webhooks.name: JobWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating webhook for batch/v1 Jobs that integrates them with Kueue's queue-based job scheduling. The mutating webhook defaults the local queue label, suspends jobs that should be managed by Kueue (based on queue name or namespace selector), and sets the managedBy field for MultiKueue. The validating webhook enforces correctness of partial admission (minParallelism annotation), sync-completion (completions-equal-parallelism annotation), and topology-aware scheduling annotations on create and update.

webhooks.name: JobWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating webhook for batch/v1 Jobs that integrates them with Kueue's queue-based job scheduling. The mutating webhook defaults the local queue label, suspends jobs that should be managed by Kueue (based on queue name or namespace selector), and sets the managedBy field for MultiKueue. The validating webhook enforces correctness of partial admission (minParallelism annotation), sync-completion (completions-equal-parallelism annotation), and topology-aware scheduling annotations on create and update.

webhooks.name: MpiJobWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating webhook for Kubeflow MPIJob resources integrated with Kueue. The mutating webhook applies default queue names, suspends jobs that should be managed by Kueue (based on queue annotation, namespace selector, or parent ownership), and sets the managedBy field. The validating webhook enforces Kueue-specific constraints on create and update, including topology-aware scheduling (TAS) pod set request validation for each MPI replica spec.

webhooks.name: MpiJobWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating webhook for Kubeflow MPIJob resources integrated with Kueue. The validating webhook enforces Kueue-specific constraints on create and update, including topology-aware scheduling (TAS) pod set request validation for each MPI replica spec.

webhooks.name: Pod-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating admission webhook for Pods managed by Kueue. On creation, it determines whether a pod should be managed by Kueue based on namespace selectors, pod selectors, queue name labels, and ancestor job ownership; if so, it adds the managed-by-kueue label, a finalizer, and a scheduling gate to suspend the pod until a Kueue workload admits it. It also validates pod group metadata consistency (group name and total count), topology-aware scheduling annotations, managed label values, and prebuilt workload naming on both create and update.

webhooks.name: PodWebhook-webhook

It also validates pod group metadata consistency (group name and total count), topology-aware scheduling annotations, managed label values, and prebuilt workload naming on both create and update.

webhooks.name: RayClusterWebhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Defaults and validates KubeRay RayCluster resources for Kueue integration. The mutating webhook assigns a default local queue, suspends jobs that should be managed by Kueue (checking ancestor ownership and namespace selectors), and sets the managedBy annotation. The validating webhook ensures autoscaling is disabled, worker group count does not exceed 7, no worker group is named 'head', and topology-aware scheduling requests are well-formed.

webhooks.name: RayClusterWebhook-webhook

webhooks.name: RayJobWebhook-webhook

webhooks.name: RayJobWebhook-webhook

webhooks.name: ResourceFlavorWebhook-webhook

webhooks.name: ResourceFlavorWebhook-webhook

webhooks.name: Webhook-webhook
webhooks.purpose: Mutating and validating admission webhook for apps/v1 Deployments managed by Kueue. The mutating webhook applies a default local queue label, walks the owner chain to detect if an ancestor job is already Kueue-managed, and if the workload should be suspended it annotates the pod template with a suspended-by-parent marker, sets Kueue-managed labels, and propagates queue-name and priority-class labels to pods. The validating webhook ensures the queue-name label is well-formed on create, and on update prevents changing or removing the queue-name while ready replicas exist and validates immutability of the workload priority class.

integration_points.name: PodGroupPodIndexLabel
integration_points.doc:
PodGroupPodIndexLabel is a label set on the Pod's metadata belonging
to a Pod group. It indicates the Pod's index within the group.

integration_points.name: PodGroupPodIndexLabelAnnotation
integration_points.doc:
PodGroupPodIndexLabelAnnotation is an annotation on the Pod's metadata
belonging to a Pod group. It indicates a label name used to retrieve
the Pod's index within the group.

integration_points.name: PodSetLabel
integration_points.doc:
PodSetLabel is a label set on the Job's PodTemplate to indicate the name
of the PodSet of the admitted Workload corresponding to the PodTemplate.
The label is set when starting the Job, and removed on stopping the Job.

integration_points.name: PodSetPreferredTopologyAnnotation
integration_points.doc:
PodSetPreferredTopologyAnnotation indicates that a PodSet requires
Topology Aware Scheduling, but scheduling all pods within pods on nodes
within the same topology domain is a preference rather than requirement.

The levels are evaluated one-by-one going up from the level indicated by
the annotation. If the PodSet cannot fit within a given topology domain
then the next topology level up is considered. If the PodSet cannot fit
at the highest topology level, then it gets admitted as distributed
among multiple topology domains.

integration_points.name: PodSetRequiredTopologyAnnotation
integration_points.doc:
PodSetRequiredTopologyAnnotation indicates that a PodSet requires
Topology Aware Scheduling, and requires scheduling all pods on nodes
within the same topology domain corresponding to the topology level
indicated by the annotation value (e.g. within a rack or within a block).

integration_points.name: PodSetUnconstrainedTopologyAnnotation
integration_points.doc:
PodSetUnconstrainedTopologyAnnotation indicates that a PodSet does not have any topology requirements.
Kueue admits the PodSet if there's enough free capacity available.
Recommended for PodSets that don't need low-latency or high-throughput pod-to-pod communication,
but want to leverage TAS capabilities improve accuracy of admitting jobs

+kubebuilder:validation:Type=boolean

integration_points.name: TASLabel
integration_points.doc:
TASLabel is a label set on the Job's PodTemplate to indicate that the
PodSet is admitted using TopologyAwareScheduling, and all Pods created
from the Job's PodTemplate also have the label. For the Pod-based
integrations the label is added in webhook during the Pod creation.

integration_points.name: TopologySchedulingGate
integration_points.doc:
TopologySchedulingGate is used to delay scheduling of a Pod until the
nodeSelectors corresponding to the assigned topology domain are injected
into the Pod. For the Pod-based integrations the gate is added in webhook
during the Pod creation.

integration_points.name: WorkloadAnnotation
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadAnnotation is an annotation set on the Job's PodTemplate to
indicate the name of the admitted Workload corresponding to the Job. The
annotation is set when starting the Job, and removed on stopping the Job.

integration_points.name: AdmissionCheckActive
integration_points.doc:
AdmissionCheckActive indicates that the controller of the admission check is
ready to evaluate the checks states

integration_points.name: AdmissionChecksSingleInstanceInClusterQueue
integration_points.doc:
AdmissionChecksSingleInstanceInClusterQueue indicates if the AdmissionCheck should be the only
one managed by the same controller (as determined by the controllerName field) in a ClusterQueue.
Having multiple AdmissionChecks managed by the same controller where at least one has this condition
set to true will cause the ClusterQueue to be marked as Inactive.

integration_points.name: CheckStatePending
integration_points.doc:
CheckStatePending means that the check still hasn't been performed and the state can be
1. Unknown, the condition was added by kueue and its controller was not able to evaluate it.
2. Set by its controller and reevaluated after quota is reserved.

integration_points.name: CheckStateRejected
integration_points.doc:
CheckStateRejected means that the check will not pass in the near future. It is not worth
to retry.
A workload having at least one check in this state will be evicted if admitted and deactivated.

integration_points.name: CheckStateRetry
integration_points.doc:
CheckStateRetry means that the check cannot pass at this moment, back off (possibly
allowing other to try, unblock quota) and retry.
A workload having at least one check in this state will be evicted if admitted and
will not be considered for admission while the check is in this state.

integration_points.name: FlavorIndependentAdmissionCheck
integration_points.doc: FlavorIndependentAdmissionCheck indicates if the AdmissionCheck cannot be applied at ResourceFlavor level.

integration_points.name: BestEffortFIFO
integration_points.doc:
BestEffortFIFO means that workloads of the same priority are ordered by creation time,
however older workloads that can't be admitted will not block
admitting newer workloads that fit existing quota.

integration_points.name: ClusterQueueActive
integration_points.doc:
ClusterQueueActive indicates that the ClusterQueue can admit new workloads and its quota
can be borrowed by other ClusterQueues in the same cohort.

integration_points.name: StrictFIFO
integration_points.doc:
StrictFIFO means that workloads of the same priority are ordered strictly by creation time.
Older workloads that can't be admitted will block admitting newer
workloads even if they fit available quota.

SecretLocationType is the name of the secret inside the namespace in which the kueue controller
manager is running. The config should be stored in the "kubeconfig" key.

Request admission check controller.

integration_points.name: InClusterQueueReason
integration_points.doc:
InClusterQueueReason indicates the Workload was preempted due to
prioritization in the ClusterQueue.

integration_points.name: InCohortFairSharingReason
integration_points.doc:
InCohortFairSharingReason indicates the Workload was preempted due to
Fair Sharing within the cohort.

integration_points.name: InCohortReclaimWhileBorrowingReason
integration_points.doc:
InCohortReclaimWhileBorrowingReason indicates the Workload was preempted
due to reclamation within the cohort while borrowing.

integration_points.name: InCohortReclamationReason
integration_points.doc:
InCohortReclamationReason indicates the Workload was preempted due to
reclamation within the Cohort.

integration_points.name: WorkloadAdmitted
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadAdmitted means that the Workload has reserved quota and all the admissionChecks
defined in the ClusterQueue are satisfied.

integration_points.name: WorkloadBackoffFinished
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadBackoffFinished indicates that the workload was requeued because
backoff finished.

integration_points.name: WorkloadClusterQueueRestarted
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadClusterQueueRestarted indicates that the workload was requeued because
cluster queue was restarted after being stopped.

integration_points.name: WorkloadDeactivated
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadDeactivated indicates that the workload was evicted
because spec.active is set to false.

integration_points.name: WorkloadDeactivationTarget
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadDeactivationTarget means that the Workload should be deactivated.
This condition is temporary, so it should be removed after deactivation.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvicted
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvicted means that the Workload was evicted. The possible reasons
for this condition are:
- "Preempted": the workload was preempted
- "PodsReadyTimeout": the workload exceeded the PodsReady timeout
- "AdmissionCheck": at least one admission check transitioned to False
- "ClusterQueueStopped": the ClusterQueue is stopped
- "Deactivated": the workload has spec.active set to false
When a workload is preempted, this condition is accompanied by the "Preempted"
condition which contains a more detailed reason for the preemption.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvictedByAdmissionCheck
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvictedByAdmissionCheck indicates that the workload was evicted
because at least one admission check transitioned to False.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvictedByClusterQueueStopped
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvictedByClusterQueueStopped indicates that the workload was evicted
because the ClusterQueue is Stopped.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvictedByDeactivation
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvictedByDeactivation indicates that the workload was evicted
because spec.active is set to false.
Deprecated: The reason is not set any longer, it is only kept temporarily to ensure
pre-existing deactivated workloads remain deactivated after upgrade from version
prior to 0.10. The reason declaration can be removed in 0.11.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvictedByLocalQueueStopped
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvictedByLocalQueueStopped indicates that the workload was evicted
because the LocalQueue is Stopped.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvictedByPodsReadyTimeout
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvictedByPodsReadyTimeout indicates that the eviction took
place due to a PodsReady timeout.

integration_points.name: WorkloadEvictedByPreemption
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadEvictedByPreemption indicates that the workload was evicted
in order to free resources for a workload with a higher priority.

integration_points.name: WorkloadFinished
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadFinished means that the workload associated to the
ResourceClaim finished running (failed or succeeded).

integration_points.name: WorkloadFinishedReasonFailed
integration_points.doc: WorkloadFinishedReasonFailed indicates that the workload's job finished with an error.

integration_points.name: WorkloadFinishedReasonOutOfSync
integration_points.doc: WorkloadFinishedReasonOutOfSync indicates that the prebuilt workload is not in sync with its parent job.

integration_points.name: WorkloadFinishedReasonSucceeded
integration_points.doc: WorkloadFinishedReasonSucceeded indicates that the workload's job finished successfully.

integration_points.name: WorkloadInadmissible
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadInadmissible means that the Workload can't reserve quota
due to LocalQueue or ClusterQueue doesn't exist or inactive.

integration_points.name: WorkloadLocalQueueRestarted
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadLocalQueueRestarted indicates that the workload was requeued because
local queue was restarted after being stopped.

integration_points.name: WorkloadMaximumExecutionTimeExceeded
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadMaximumExecutionTimeExceeded indicates that the workload exceeded its
maximum execution time.

integration_points.name: WorkloadPreempted
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadPreempted means that the Workload was preempted.
The possible values of the reason field are "InClusterQueue", "InCohort".
In the future more reasons can be introduced, including those conveying
more detailed information. The more detailed reasons should be prefixed
by one of the "base" reasons.

integration_points.name: WorkloadQuotaReserved
integration_points.doc: WorkloadQuotaReserved means that the Workload has reserved quota a ClusterQueue.

integration_points.name: WorkloadReactivated
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadReactivated indicates that the workload was requeued because
spec.active is set to true after deactivation.

integration_points.name: WorkloadRecovered
integration_points.doc: WorkloadRecovered indicates that after at least one Pod has failed, the Workload has recovered and is running

integration_points.name: WorkloadRequeued
integration_points.doc: WorkloadRequeued means that the Workload was requeued due to eviction.

integration_points.name: WorkloadRequeuingLimitExceeded
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadRequeuingLimitExceeded indicates that the workload exceeded max number
of re-queuing retries.

integration_points.name: WorkloadStarted
integration_points.doc: WorkloadStarted indicates that all Pods are ready and the Workload has successfully started

integration_points.name: WorkloadWaitForRecovery
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadWaitForRecovery indicates the reason for the PodsReady=False condition
when the Pods were ready since the workload admission, but some pod has failed,
and workload waits for recovering.

integration_points.name: WorkloadWaitForStart
integration_points.doc:
WorkloadWaitForStart indicates the reason for PodsReady=False condition
when the pods have not been ready since admission, or the workload is not admitted.

	import (

	kclientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(c)
	_ = aggregatorclientsetscheme.AddToScheme(clientsetscheme.Scheme)

After this, RawExtensions in Kubernetes types will serialize kube-aggregator types
correctly.

integration_points.name: CQStatusActive
integration_points.doc:
CQStatusActive means the ClusterQueue can admit new workloads and its quota
can be borrowed by other ClusterQueues in the cohort.

integration_points.name: CQStatusPending
integration_points.doc:
CQStatusPending means the ClusterQueue is accepted but not yet active,
this can be because of:
- a missing ResourceFlavor referenced by the ClusterQueue
- a missing or inactive AdmissionCheck referenced by the ClusterQueue
- the ClusterQueue is stopped
In this state, the ClusterQueue can't admit new workloads and its quota can't be borrowed
by other active ClusterQueues in the cohort.

integration_points.name: CQStatusTerminating
integration_points.doc: CQStatusTerminating means the clusterQueue is in pending deletion.
